people.paul.role: Writer in chains who asks Timothy to come soon
people.paul.relations: He calls Timothy his beloved child. He asks Timothy to bring Mark, a cloak, and the books.
people.paul.meaning: Paul writes in chains and tells Timothy not to be ashamed. He says his time of departure has come. He lists who left him and who stayed. He asks Timothy to come before winter. He asks for his cloak, the books, and Mark.
people.timothy.role: Paul’s beloved child, told to preach and endure
people.timothy.relations: Paul calls him his beloved child. His grandmother Lois and mother Eunice had sincere faith.
people.timothy.meaning: Paul remembers Timothy’s tears and his family’s faith. He tells Timothy to guard sound teaching and to endure hardship. He tells him to preach the word and to correct others gently. Paul asks him to come soon.
people.jesus.role: Lord who will judge, and who stood by Paul
people.jesus.relations: Paul calls him our Lord and Savior. Paul says he is risen and of David’s offspring.
people.jesus.meaning: Paul tells Timothy to remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead. Paul says the Lord will judge the living and the dead. Paul says the Lord stood by him at his first defense. Paul expects the Lord to deliver him into his heavenly Kingdom.
people.titus.role: Worker who has gone to Dalmatia
people.titus.relations: Paul names him with Demas, who went to Thessalonica, and Crescens, who went to Galatia.
people.titus.meaning: Paul says Titus went to Dalmatia. The verse gives no reason and no task. It is one of three departures Paul lists as he asks Timothy to come.
people.tychicus.relations: Paul names him just after asking Timothy to bring Mark.
people.tychicus.meaning: Paul says he sent Tychicus to Ephesus. The letter gives no reason. The note comes between the request to bring Mark and the request for the cloak.
places.rome.summary: Onesiphorus was in Rome in chapter 1. He looked hard for Paul there and found him.
places.rome.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.ephesus.summary: Onesiphorus served at Ephesus, as Timothy knows well (chapter 1). Paul says he sent Tychicus to Ephesus (chapter 4).
places.ephesus.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.corinth.summary: Paul says Erastus stayed at Corinth, in his closing notes in chapter 4.
places.corinth.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
sources.web.summary: The full Scripture text is the main text for original close readings.
sources.web.limits: Paul is the named writer. The guide did not check authorship, dates, Greek forms, or manuscripts. It did not match the travel notices into one full plan. No exact prison site is given.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-44.summary: The lesson links courage, Scripture, and steady teaching.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-44.limits: Second Timothy coverage follows what the lesson discusses in chapters one, three, and four. The guide did not check the linked talks or Restoration passages.
sources.skinner-timothy.summary: Skinner stresses that Scripture helps faithful service and patient teaching.
sources.skinner-timothy.limits: This is Skinner’s own reading. The guide did not check his Greek analysis or his authorship discussion. That discussion is linked elsewhere. It did not check any rebuilt history of how Scripture formed.
sources.net-acts-map.summary: Opening descriptions and coordinates mark the cities named in Acts.
sources.net-acts-map.limits: These broad points do not confirm ancient events, travel paths, buildings, or coastlines. The guide did not adopt older encyclopedia claims about authorship, law, population, or exact dates.
